summary: Backend-only iteration focused on the two new features added this session: FCM device-token registration (POST /api/push/register-device, /api/push/unregister-device) and the built-in bill-due dunning reminders (GET /api/reminders/preview, /api/reminders/dunning-list; POST /api/reminders/send) after the UPPERCASE bill-status fix. Added /app/backend/tests/test_push_reminders.py (16 focused tests) and re-ran the full suite. Result: 46 passed + 1 xpassed / 47 (100%). All target endpoints behave as specified: register-device returns {ok:true, fcm_enabled:true} for tokens ≥20 chars and 400 for shorter, unregister deletes cleanly, /reminders/preview now returns non-empty stageable bills from seed data (confirming the UPPERCASE fix on _bill_stage + queries), dunning-list returns stage_label without error, /reminders/send returns {ok:true, sent:N>0} and the second call returns sent=0 (dedup via reminder_log works). All auth-protected endpoints (/rooms, /tenants, /bills) still return 401 without a token; /reminders/preview and /reminders/dunning-list also enforce auth at the router level (verified via curl on public URL → 401).

minor.issue: No explicit Depends(get_current_user) in the function signatures (relies on router-level global auth). They ARE protected in the running deployment (returns 401 on public URL), but the source reads as if they were open – anyone reviewing the handler in isolation would miss it. Add explicit Depends for clarity and defense-in-depth.

$in filter still includes legacy lowercase ('unpaid','partially_paid') alongside the current UPPERCASE values. Harmless but keeps dead-status support alive; consider dropping once a data migration confirms no lowercase docs remain.

Skips silently when no tenant user account exists for a bill (acct=None). Any seeded bill for a tenant without a portal login is invisible to the sweep even though preview lists it – counts of preview vs sent can diverge. Log a warning at least.
asyncio.sleep(21600)=6h fixed interval with bare except:pass swallows every error including CancelledError – makes shutdown/debugging harder. Log the exception.

action_items: (Optional) Add explicit Depends(get_current_user) + owner/admin role check to /api/reminders/preview and /api/reminders/dunning-list for source-level clarity.
(Optional) Log skipped bills in run_reminder_sweep when tenant user account is missing so operators know why preview count > sent count.
(Optional) Remove legacy lowercase status entries from the reminders $in filters now that the schema is UPPERCASE.
critical_code_review_comments: Three near-identical bill queries (dunning-list, send-whatsapp-batch, run_reminder_sweep, preview) each duplicate the status $in filter and the _bill_stage loop; extract a helper `_stageable_bills()` to avoid drift the next time statuses change.
send_fcm_to_user swallowing INVALID_ARGUMENT is fine, but auto-removing tokens should also emit an audit entry so admins can see churn.
server.py is now >4100 lines – unchanged since iter 3, still needs router split.
seed_data_creation: Session-scoped autouse fixture reseeds via POST /api/seed → {rooms:7, tenants:4, bills:9, tickets:3, tokens:3}.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_push_reminders.py; run with `pytest backend/tests/ -p no:randomly`. Both push and reminders features are working end-to-end. The dedup test asserts second /api/reminders/send returns sent=0, so if you add tests that further mutate reminder_log or bills between the send calls, keep them AFTER TestReminders or reset state. FCM_ENABLED=True with real service account for project lewihouse-7a0d7 – endpoint returns fcm_enabled:true but we intentionally do not send to a real device.
rca_of_the_issue: Prior bug (reminders never firing) confirmed fixed: _bill_stage + the three bill queries now match UPPERCASE statuses UNPAID/PARTIAL_PAID/OVERDUE (kept lowercase in $in for legacy safety). preview returns seeded overdue rows and /reminders/send successfully increments the sent counter and populates reminder_log so the next call dedups to 0.
